responses.value: Install carbon capture. A government credit of $85 a ton on 1 million tons a year pays $85M a year for 12 years, far above the $15M running cost, so the $200M pays back in about 3 years, and two states will require low-carbon cement for public projects from 2028. The main risk is that the credit is cut or repealed. The next step is to sign a binding credit agreement before committing.
Update. At $20 a ton the credit pays $20M, only $5M over running costs, so I'd hold off on the $200M.
